text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The ministerial group on privatisation agreed at its meeting yesterday, under Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, to offer for sale shares in 18 companies and joint-venture banks with a value of 2.2 billion pounds ($650 million). Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said that the companies were in industry, agriculture, housing and tourism. Some are already listed on the stock exchange, he added. The industrial companies are: Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries, Chloride Egypt, Alexandria National Iron and Steel (ANSDK), Misr Gulf Oil Processing (MIGOP), Suez Cement and Aracemco/Arab Ceramic. Other companies are Cairo Poultry, Egyptian Engineers Arab Realty Investment, Misr Development, Tourism Urbanisation (Jolieville), Semiramis Hotels and Ismailia Tourism. The joint-venture banks are Suez Canal Bank, Misr International Bank/MIBANK, Egyptian American Bank (EAB), Egyptian Saudi Finance Bank, Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank and National Investment Bank.
- President Mubarak attended an armed forces iftar at infantry headquarters.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa had talks with PLO official Farouk Kaddoumi on aspects of the peace process. Moussa said they discussed refugees, Jerusalem, Jewish settlements and self-determination.

- It has been decided to take immediate measures after the Eid to put an end to losses in 22 public-sector companies before June. Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said the measures include winding up the loss-making activities, without affecting the rights of workers. The state will either find other jobs for them or give them early retirement. The companies may also lease the low-profitability activities to improve profitability.

- Four people have been charged in connection with the collapse of a building in Heliopolis last October, killing 64 people. The charges include gross negligence and the penalties could be imprisonment with hard labour.
- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib was taken to hospital after he was taken ill at an iftar on Wednesday evening. He had a sudden loss of blood pressure but is now stable.
- Foreign Minister Moussa sid that continuing Israeli settlement activity and selling flats to settlers was annoying and serious. He said Israel should have sold the flats to Palestinian refugees.
- The State Security prosecutor has released 23 members of the Satanist group on bail.
- The general assemblies of 16 state holding companies start today under Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid to fix the share of profits workers will receive.
